narrative:
The model estimated a 51.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that is just over the halfway mark, the prediction was classified as a likely failure, and your application was denied. This is a narrow risk estimate, not a certainty that you cannot succeed.

The strongest factor was your third-year class decile. At 1.00, compared with an average of 5.79 among accepted students, it was the most influential factor and pushed the prediction toward bar failure. Your LSAT score was second in importance. At 36, slightly below the accepted-student average of 37.18, it nevertheless worked in your favor and pushed toward passing. Your undergraduate GPA was third; at 3.40, above the accepted average of 3.23, it also pushed toward passing. Those positive signals were not enough to offset the third-year decile concern.

Gender and race were not used in the prediction. To improve future applications, ask admissions for feedback, consider retaking the LSAT if you can raise your score, and provide context or evidence of stronger recent academic performance. A later application cycle or additional schools may better present your chances.
